content.user_title: Extract Security Requirements from Threat Models
content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to turn threat analysis into clear implementation work. This skill converts threats and business context into traceable requirements, user stories, tests, and compliance mappings.
actual_capabilities: Defines a security requirement model with priority, domain, traceability, acceptance criteria, and test case fields.
Maps STRIDE threat categories to security domains and reusable requirement patterns.
Generates security user story text, epics, acceptance criteria, and security test cases from requirements.
Creates threat-to-requirement traceability matrices for requirement sets.
Maps requirements to PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, and OWASP control references.
Identifies compliance gaps and weak control coverage from a requirement set.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and Python examples, not a packaged command-line tool.
Generated requirements depend on the quality and completeness of the supplied threat model.
Compliance mappings are starter references and still need review by qualified compliance owners.
It does not verify whether implemented controls satisfy the generated requirements.

use_cases.title: Convert Threat Models Into Backlog Items
use_cases.description: Transform STRIDE findings into specific security requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria for delivery planning.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Traceability
use_cases.description: Map security requirements to common control frameworks and identify missing or weak coverage areas.

use_cases.title: Create Security Test Plans
use_cases.description: Turn each requirement into testable criteria and verification ideas for engineering and quality assurance workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Basic Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small threat list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert these threats into security requirements. Include requirement titles, domains, priorities, rationale, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Write Security User Stories
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn requirements into agile-ready work items.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert these security requirements into user stories. Include acceptance criteria, definition of done, and traceability to the original threats.

prompt_templates.title: Map Requirements to Compliance
prompt_templates.scenario: Create audit support from a requirement set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map these security requirements to PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, and OWASP references. Identify gaps and weak coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Complete Security Requirement Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for planning, testing, and compliance output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a complete security requirement package from this threat model and business context. Include requirements, user stories, test cases, priorities, traceability, compliance mappings, and gap analysis.

output_examples.input: A threat model lists spoofing and tampering risks for an account settings service.
output: Security requirements for authentication, session management, input validation, and data integrity.
Acceptance criteria that require authentication checks, validated input, and monitored modification attempts.
Test cases for unauthenticated access, invalid credentials, forged sessions, and tampered data.

output_examples.input: A team needs compliance traceability for payment and user profile requirements.
output: A control mapping across PCI DSS, GDPR, and OWASP domains.
A list of missing controls where no requirement provides coverage.
Weak coverage notes where only one requirement supports an important control.

output_examples.input: A product owner needs delivery-ready security stories for a sprint plan.
output: Security user stories grouped by domain and priority.
Definitions of done that include implementation, tests, review, and documentation.
Traceability notes that connect each story to threats and compliance references.

best_practices: Start with clear threat IDs, affected assets, impact, likelihood, and target components.
Review generated requirements with engineering, product, security, and compliance stakeholders.
Keep threat references, acceptance criteria, and test cases linked through delivery and review.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad statements like be secure as final requirements.
Do not treat generated compliance mappings as legal or audit approval.
Do not skip testability, ownership, or priority when adding requirements to a backlog.

faq.question: What inputs work best with this skill?
faq.answer: Threat models with IDs, categories, targets, impact, likelihood, and business context produce the clearest requirements.

faq.question: Can it create agile user stories?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates for security user stories, acceptance criteria, definitions of done, and security test cases.

faq.question: Does it support compliance mapping?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes example mappings for PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, and OWASP control references.

faq.question: Does it run security scans?
faq.answer: No. It helps define requirements and tests, but it does not scan code or validate implemented controls.

faq.question: Can teams customize the requirement categories?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples are structured so teams can adapt domains, priorities, frameworks, and templates.

faq.question: Is legal review still needed for regulated systems?
faq.answer: Yes. Compliance references should be reviewed by qualified security, legal, or audit owners.
